verdict.rationale: Crossplane's own CLI documents rendering Composition Functions without a cluster (crossplane-docs-7), so users can see what resources a composition would produce before applying it. Nothing shows a plan-style diff against live state that classifies creates, updates and destroys. The `helm install --dry-run` item is a Helm feature for installing Crossplane itself, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: a diff against existing cluster/cloud state, explicit create/update/destroy classification, a documented plan-then-apply workflow, independent or hands-on corroboration.
